title: Add lightweight dual-encoder + compact cross reranker: pinning, profiling, and catalog publication
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Goal: Bring a new lightweight dual-encoder embedding model (dual-encoder-lite v0.9) and a compact cross-attention reranker (mini-cross v0.3) through Redwood's onboarding, deterministic version pinning, and performance profile publication pipeline. The models target mobile/edge-friendly retrieval workflows where token-latency and per-request cost must be minimized while keeping semantic quality within a 5% degradation vs current prod reranker for short queries. This ticket covers artifact ingestion, automated compatibility checks, offline and online profiling across representative traffic envelopes, creation of catalog entries with pinned versions, and publishing performance profiles to the model catalog used by routing policies. Success criteria: (1) profiles published to catalog with validated quantization path (8-bit/4-bit recommended configs), (2) pinned artifact manifest and compatibility checks pass in CI, (3) latency and throughput meet the target SLOs on dedicated-small GPU fleet and on CPU-quantized fallback, (4) documented rollout plan and rollback tickets added to release checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Artifact ingestion pipeline stores dual-encoder-lite v0.9 and mini-cross v0.3 in model-bucket with correct metadata and checksums
Automated compatibility tests (manifest schema, tokenizer mapping, KV cache shape) pass in CI for both CPU and GPU variants
Performance profiles (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, VRAM usage, cost per 1M tokens) are published to catalog and visible in console under 'profiling/embeddings' and 'profiling/rerankers'
Pin manifest created and propagated to serving runtime so routing can select pinned versions under 'experimental:dual-lite' policy
Canary rollout runs with 10% traffic for 48 hours with production telemetry: no regressions in downstream relevance signals beyond defined threshold (<=5% drop)
steps: 1) Validate artifact packaging: model weights, tokenizer, manifest.json, example inputs/outputs
2) Run offline eval harness with internal query set (synthetic + sampled prod prompts) to record base quality and latency baselines
3) Run quantization experiments (dynamic 8-bit, static 4-bit where supported) and capture perf/memory tradeoffs
4) Create pin manifest and update catalog entry draft with recommended runtime flags and quantization profile
5) Submit PR to onboarding pipeline and request infra review for CVM compatibility
6) Launch controlled canary on dedicated-small pool and monitor SLOs + quality metrics for 48 hours
7) Publish profile bundle (v0.9-v0.3) to catalog and add rollout playbook to Console release artifacts
comments: 2026-02-18 Sofia Chen: Created ticket. Initial feasibility notes: dual-encoder-lite uses fused attention blocks that require updated kernel selector for aarch64; mini-cross is sensitive to KV cache layout and prefers continuous batching. Proposed to run first-pass offline profiles on dedicated-small (A10x1) and CPU quantized on c6i-large.

2026-02-23 Miguel Alvarez: Completed artifact packaging and manifest draft. Found tokenizer mismatch for multi-lingual fallback; added token mapping shim. Uploaded artifacts to s3://models/dual-lite/v0.9/ and s3://models/mini-cross/v0.3/ (links in PR).

2026-03-01 QA: Offline eval results uploaded. Dual-lite achieves 92% of baseline nDCG on short queries with 40% lower median latency; mini-cross reaches 97% nDCG but uses 30% more VRAM in default FP16. Attached preliminary tables in Drive link.

2026-03-04 Infra feedback: Kernel selection needs a small patch to avoid suboptimal GEMM on A10 for sequence length 64. ENG-70121 will include a minimal runtime hint flag --force-kernel=matmul-v2 to be used in canary.

2026-03-07 Miguel Alvarez: Quantization experiments done. Dynamic 8-bit gives best latency/memory balance for dual-lite; mini-cross needs hybrid 8-bit for keys/values and FP16 for attention to retain quality. Updated profile JSONs and added note about fallback to CPU quantized if GPU allocation unavailable.

2026-03-10 Sofia Chen: Started catalog entry draft and pin manifest generation. Opening PR to publish profiles and pin manifests. Planning canary launch next week (2026-03-15) for 48h with 10% traffic. Added rollback criteria and monitoring dashboard links to PR description.
notes: Technical trade-offs: prioritized latency/cost for dual-encoder-lite at the expense of small quality drop on long-tail queries; mini-cross prioritized quality with slightly higher VRAM requirement so pairs well as a reranker in two-stage pipelines.

Rollout plan: canary->gradual ramp to 50% over two days if quality SLOs hold; otherwise rollback to pinned older reranker manifest and run A/B analysis. Coordinate with Solutions Eng for customers on Dedicated who opted into 'experimental' routing.
Observability: added console traces for model variant, quantization flag, and kernel selection to aid post-mortem if regressions occur.
